chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, that al-Ridha (peace be upon him) wrote to him:

Indeed Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) was the trustee of Allah among His creation. When he (peace be upon him and his family) passed away, we, the People of the House, were his inheritors. Thus we are the trustees of Allah in His earth.

With us is the knowledge of calamities and deaths, the lineages of the Arabs, and the origin of Islam. And indeed we recognize the man when we see him, by the reality of his faith and the reality of his hypocrisy. And indeed our Shia are recorded with their names and the names of their fathers. Allah took the covenant upon us and upon them — they shall arrive where we arrive and enter where we enter. There is none upon the nation of Islam other than us and them.

We are the noble ones, the saved ones; we are the vanguard of the prophets; we are the sons of the successors; we are those singled out in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; we are the most entitled of all people to the Book of Allah; and we are the most entitled of all people to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).
And we are those for whom Allah legislated His religion, and He said in His Book:

'He has legislated for you, O Family of Muhammad, from the religion what He enjoined upon Noah' — He has enjoined upon us what He enjoined upon Noah — 'and that which We revealed to you, O Muhammad, and what We enjoined upon Ibrahim, Musa, and Isa.'

So He has taught us and conveyed to us the knowledge of what we know, and has entrusted to us their knowledge. We are the inheritors of the Determined Ones (Ulu al-Azm) from among the Messengers: 'Establish the religion, O Family of Muhammad, and do not be divided therein' — and be united as one community. Hard it is for the polytheists — those who associate others with the wilayah of Ali — what you call them to from the wilayah of Ali. Allah, O Muhammad, guides to Himself whoever turns in repentance, whoever answers your call toward the wilayah of Ali (peace be upon him).

key_terms.أُمَنَاءُ اللَّهِ: Trustees of Allah — the Imams as divinely appointed guardians of religion and knowledge
key_terms.أُولُو الْعَزْمِ: The Determined Ones — the five greatest Prophets (Noah, Ibrahim, Moses, Jesus, Muhammad)
key_terms.النُّجَبَاءُ: The noble ones — elite persons of high spiritual station
key_terms.الْبَلَايَا وَالْمَنَايَا: Calamities and deaths — esoteric knowledge of future events possessed by the Imams
key_terms.الْمِيثَاق: The Covenant — the primordial covenant between Allah and the souls of humanity
key_terms.وَلَايَة: Wilayah — divinely appointed guardianship and authority; here specifically of Imam Ali (AS)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ridha say about the Ahl al-Bayt being heirs to prophetic knowledge?
ai.summary: This is a letter from Imam al-Ridha (AS) to his trusted companion Abdullah ibn Jundab, asserting the supreme status of the Ahl al-Bayt as divinely appointed trustees and inheritors of prophetic knowledge. The Imam establishes that after the Prophet's death, the Ahl al-Bayt became the sole legitimate guardians of Islam, possessing knowledge of calamities, lineages, and the capacity to perceive true faith and hypocrisy. The letter culminates in citing Quran 42:13 to affirm that the divine covenant given to all the Determined Prophets — Noah, Muhammad, Ibrahim, Moses, and Jesus — was transmitted to and inherited by the Imams, with wilayah of Ali as its central pillar.
